text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- The inflexible position of Estonia could halt the Estonian-Russian border talks and postpone the border agreement, Vassili Svirin, leader of the Russian delegation, announced after two-day negotiations in Tallinn.
POSTIMEES
- The number of jobs in Koeru district, central Estonia, has fallen from 1,130 to 200 after the bankruptcy of the area's four main employers. The local council fears a social explosion.

- Meetings at northeastern Oru where the peat factory has gone bankrupt between workers and district officials have not brought results and the situation remains tense. An adviser to the prime minister will meet the protesting workers tomorrow.
- A major business project of one billion dollars, a cellulose factory, was the real cause of the fight for power in Tartu, political analyst Rein Toomla said.
- The privatisation of the Kiviter chemical plant may continue with a new round in two weeks, the director of the Privatisation Agency Vaino Sarnet said.
SONUMILEHT
- The events of the Cultural Festival of Nordic Countries in Tallinn include exhibitions, concerts, workshops and film.

- Estonia may be the first country in Europe where the OSCE ends its mission because the integration of the Russian-speaking population has reached its final stage, Estonian Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves told the OSCE council in Vienna.

- The Bank of Estonia has signed numerous bad loans with commercial banks in Estonia in the last three years and has not got its money back, state audit officials said in their report on the central bank.
- Parliament was not informed that ex-PM Tiit Vaehi was to meet Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeni Primakov. It proves that democratic institutions in Estonia are still weak, MP Kristiina Ojuland said.
- Initiators of the Helsinki-Tallinn tunnel presented a preliminary project to the public in Helsinki. The cost of the project is estimated at one billion kroons.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- Specialists investigating the fire at the Halinga home for elderly in Parnu suspect that either smoking or faulty electric wiring caused the fire.
- Teachers of 17 schools in Tallinn decided to hold a strike on May 12 if they do not receive a promised pay-rise.
ARIPAEV
- The Meat Processing Plant in Paide central Estonia was restarted after a two-year halt and is filling orders for sausages for Russia, the management said.
